summary: Ephemeral environment JIT access broken after role rename due to authz-cache invalidation bug
description:
Issue summary:
Ephemeral (just-in-time) environment provisioning for several developer sandboxes intermittently fails to grant access after recent role renames/migrations. Attempts to assume newly named roles return 403 from auth-proxy despite the role existing and bindings being correct in both GCP and AWS accounts.

Impact:
- Developers cannot access freshly provisioned sandboxes in staging; workflows blocked for ~10 engineers intermittently.
- Affects CI-driven ephemeral runs that depend on cross-cloud STS bridging.
- No customer-facing impact, but blocks internal debugging and release testing.

Environment:
- Staging account pair: GCP project redwood-staging-ml (us-west1) -> AWS account redwood-staging-ops (us-west-2) via WIF -> AssumeRole chain.
- Auth-proxy v1.9.4 deployed in staging (pods: auth-proxy-5 replicas).
- Recent role rename performed 2026-03-09 as part of cleanup (old name: llm-debugger-role -> new name: llm-devops-debug-role).

Steps to reproduce:
1. Trigger ephemeral env creation via infra-scripts (create-ephemeral --env=staging --team=llm).
2. Observe infra-scripts call auth-proxy to exchange WIF token and request an STS AssumeRole.
3. Auth-proxy responds 403 with body: "role binding mismatch".
4. Manually running aws sts assume-role with the same principal succeeds after purging the auth-proxy cache or restarting one replica.

Observed behavior:
- Failures are intermittent (succeeds for some users/requests, fails for others).
- Restarting a single auth-proxy pod temporarily causes the failing requests to succeed for ~15 minutes.

Expected behavior:
- After role rename and propagation, auth-proxy should respect IAM bindings and allow JIT assume-role requests without manual cache purge.

Logs / Attachments:
- Excerpt from auth-proxy logs (2026-03-11T14:22:03Z): "[WARN] cache_miss but allow check failed: principal=openid:user:dev@example.com truncated_id=dev@example; role=llm-devops-debug-role; decision=DENY"
- GCP workload identity binding audit: lines included showing binding exists with full principal.
- Kube events: no RBAC denies.

Notes:
- This looks related to a cache key encoding change deployed 2026-03-09 (auth-proxy PR 1279) which started hashing service account emails by splitting at the first '@' to shorten keys. Hypothesis: the truncation created collisions or mismatches with newly created role sessions/STS audience strings, preventing correct lookup and invalidating policy checks.

2026-03-10 10:05 - Miguel Torres (Infra): Investigating. I can reproduce locally by renaming a role and creating ephemeral envs; one auth-proxy replica shows DENY while others allow. Suspect cache key collision. Adding Priya for SRE input.

2026-03-10 13:42 - Priya Rao (SRE): Observed auth-proxy metrics: cache.hit_rate drops on rollout and returns to normal after ~20 minutes. Restart of a replica flushes its in-memory cache leading to temporary success. No network errors seen.
Action: will add temporary admin endpoint to flush caches to unblock teams while we diagnose.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Miguel Torres (Infra): Confirmed PR 1279 changed key derivation. Reproduced collision where two principals map to same truncated key when there is a dot in local-part. Patch underway to use full hashed UID instead of truncated local-part. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/1283
2026-03-12 17:55 - Security (Nina Gomez): Need to ensure any cache key change does not leak full email in logs. Use one-way hash with salt per-environment. Follow-up in Confluence checklist updated.

2026-03-13 09:10 - Miguel Torres (Infra): Hotfix deployed to staging auth-proxy (v1.9.5) with hashed uid cache key (non-reversible) and a cache invalidation endpoint. Monitoring for 48h. Marking ticket as in-progress; will update once stable.

2026-03-13 12:40 - Aisha Patel (Support): Workaround documented and communicated to devs: restart one auth-proxy pod or call POST /admin/flush-caches. Added instructions to internal Slack #infra-support.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-09: auth-proxy PR 1279 rolled to staging (key shortening).
- 2026-03-10: first reports of intermittent failures.
Hypotheses tested:
- Network/AWS API flakiness: ruled out via direct sts calls.
- RBAC in k8s: ruled out.
- Cache key collisions due to truncation of principal identifiers: reproduced and confirmed.
Technical finding:
- auth-proxy used local-part truncation for cache keys to limit memory footprint. This produced collisions when renames or certain local-part formats (dots, plus tags) produced duplicate truncated strings. The policy lookup used the truncated key leading to stale/incorrect allow decisions.
Mitigations tried:
- Rolling restart of proxy pods (temporary fix).
- Adding in-flight cache flush admin endpoint to allow immediate invalidation.
resolution_notes:
Temporary workaround:
- Admins can call POST /admin/flush-caches on auth-proxy service or restart a replica to clear in-memory cache. Documented in Confluence runbook link above.
Permanent fix deployed to staging (2026-03-13):
- auth-proxy v1.9.5 uses SHA256(salt + full-uid) as cache key (no PII in logs), removing truncation collisions.
- Added automated cache invalidation hook in infra-scripts to flush auth-proxy caches after IAM role migrations or renames.
- PRs: auth-proxy#1283 (key change), infra-scripts#902 (post-migration flush).
Follow-ups / action items:
- Roll the fix to prod after validation (SRE signoff).
- Add integration test to role rename CI path to validate cache invalidation (owner: infra-team).
- Update the IAM migration checklist to include auth-proxy cache flush step.
- Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-18 to capture learnings and timeline.
Status: fix in staging; monitoring shows no reoccurrences since 2026-03-13 10:00 UTC.
